To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

immunization with the capsid-modified, replication-deficient adenovirus vector AdC7 expressing the P. aeruginosao outer membrane protein F induces robust P. aerugionosa-specific systemic and lung mucosal immunity that effectively clears P. aerugionsa from the lungs in mice and rats.
immunization with Ad5OprF.RGDRGD induces robust anti-Pseudomonads immune responses that effectively clear P. aeruginosas from the lungs of immunized mice.

immunization with Adenovirus vector-based vaccine AdC7OpreF.RGD induces potent immune responses in mice, rats and cystic fibrosis mice and that immunization with the vaccine AdC7OPreF.RGD clears Pseudomonas infection from the lungs in mice, rats, and cystic fibroses mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a vaccine to control P. aeruginosainfections, in particular in patients with CF, by using a replication-deficient, primate-based Ad vector expressing P. aeruginosasurface antigen OprF.
the development of an adenoviral vaccine for the treatment and prevention of P. aerugionsa infection.
the development of an adenovirus-based vaccine that is effective in clearing an already established Pseudomonas infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AdC7.OprF.RGD vaccine has the potential to be used in the clinical situation to treat P. aeruginos infections.
the data presented in this manuscript suggest that the capsid modified AdC7OPrF.RGD vaccine can be effective as post-exposure vaccine in a mouse model of P. aerugenosa respiratory infection.

the results of the present study show that post-exposure immunization of mice, CF mice and rats with AdC7.OprF.RGD leads to enhanced anti-Pseudomonal immune responses and increased elimination of P. aerugionsa from the respiratory tract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AdC7 vector can induce protective immunity against respiratory infection with P. aerugionosa in mice, CF mice and rats.
the AdC7 vector is an effective vector for post-exposure immunization against Pseudomonas infections in mice, rats and humans.
AdC7.OprF.RGD is a potent inducers of lung mucosal, hummal and cellular immune responses that can be used for post-exposure immunization to clear P. aeruginos respiratory infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a replication-deficient adenovirus vector expressing the P. aeruginogus OprF antigen is able to clear an established P. aeroginosa respiratory infection in wild-type, CF and Sprague Dawely rats.
AdC7-based vectors are promising vaccine platforms for post-exposure immunization against P. aerugenosa infection in the lungs.

intranasal immunizations of mice, rats and CF mice with a replication-deficient adenovirus expressing the P. aeruginosae outer membrane protein F, AdC7OfrF.RGD, can clear an established P. aerugenosa lung infection.
